title: Machine learning helps identify a Beclin 2-Ubiquilin 1 interaction in breast-cancer cells
summary: Classical machine-learning classifiers predicted autophagy-related protein interactions, which researchers intersected with immunoprecipitation-mass-spectrometry results to select candidates in triple-negative breast-cancer cells. Co-immunoprecipitation supported the Beclin 2-Ubiquilin 1 interaction, and cell experiments linked Beclin 2 overexpression to increased Ubiquilin 1, autophagy and reduced proliferation and migration. Despite the title, the reported classifiers are Naive Bayes, decision trees and k-nearest neighbors; the results do not establish clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Naive Bayes; decision tree; k-nearest neighbors
organization: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Sichuan University

evidence.tested: Co-immunoprecipitation supported the predicted Beclin 2-Ubiquilin 1 interaction; subsequent MDA-MB-231 cell assays examined autophagy, proliferation and migration.
evidence.unknown: The represented result is from cell experiments, not clinical treatment. Predicted interaction counts are not experimentally confirmed interaction counts.
evidence.ai_role: Naive Bayes, decision-tree and k-nearest-neighbor classifiers predicted protein interactions; predictions were intersected with experimentally detected Beclin 2-associated proteins before targeted validation.

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, result-specific experiments, discussion, affiliations and journal publication metadata; no independent replication performed.
